newsitem.title: CHILE: Iansa sees $230 mln in new investments.
newsitem.headline: Iansa sees $230 mln in new investments.

text.p: Chilean foodmaker Industria Azucarera Nacional SA, or Iansa, plans to invest $230 million between now and the year 2000, mainly in Chile and in tomato production in Brazil, general manager Ernesto Sahr said.
Plans for the Brazilian investment, including a $25 million tomato processing plant, will probably be finished by the end of this year, Sahr told reporters.
Iansa has said in the past it plans a capital increase through American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

Iansa was still looking at various investment prospects in Argentina despite the trouble it had with a bid for sugar refinery San Martn de Tabacal in the Argentine province of Salta in June, said Sahr.
"We're looking at some possibilities (in Argentina) but there is still no news," he said.

Iansa won the bidding for San Martn de Tabacal when it was privatized. But almost immediately after the bidding, Iansa said it was withdrawing its winning offer because Iansa accountants had not had time to examine the refinery's finances closely.
The company's bid, $29 million, turned out to be nearly three times what the next highest bidder offered, Iansa said at the time.
Because of the mixup, Iansa lost a $3 million deposit it had to pay to bid for the Argentine company, according to Iansa.
